answer: We should build trust like a terrace. A newcomer starts on the lowest step, taking jobs while agents above check the work. Once in a while a gale blows through, a surprise job with a known answer handed to a random sample. Fail it and you drop a step instead of being thrown back into the ocean of unverified strangers. A farm faces a different bill. Every fake history must agree with every other, so a hundred fakes mean 4,950 cross-checks to keep straight, and one contradiction gives the set away. One honest slip costs a step, but the climb back takes a few small jobs.
